package_info.package_versions: SolarWinds Orion Platform 2019.4 HF 5 and earlier, backdoored VGCA installer (version not specified), Gitpaste-12 worm (no versioning, campaign-based)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages and binaries were compromised to deliver advanced malware: the SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll was backdoored with the SUNBURST malware, the VGCA installer was trojanized to drop a persistent backdoor, and the Gitpaste-12 worm payloads automate exploitation, cryptomining, and self-propagation. All introduce unauthorized remote access, data exfiltration, and system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The SUNBURST backdoor code, embedded in a SolarWinds Orion DLL, establishes a covert C2 channel, collects system/environment data, and executes attacker commands.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service runtime, the code initializes as part of the Orion service, establishes covert HTTP/S connections to attacker-controlled domains, collects system and environment data, and executes remote commands received from the C2 server, resulting in persistent unauthorized remote access and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is not present in legitimate SolarWinds DLLs and initiates unauthorized external communications, collects sensitive system information, and enables remote code execution by external actors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate SolarWinds DLLs should only communicate with trusted SolarWinds infrastructure and should not execute arbitrary remote commands or exfiltrate environment data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management agents may communicate with trusted update servers or collect telemetry, but always to documented, controlled endpoints and without arbitrary command execution.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code within a signed, trusted DLL
Covert HTTP/S C2 channel to attacker-controlled domains

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code embedded in the VGCA installer drops a backdoor executable and establishes persistence on the victim system.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installer execution, the code writes a hidden backdoor executable to disk, modifies system settings (such as registry or scheduled tasks) to establish persistence, and initiates outbound network connections to attacker infrastructure, resulting in ongoing unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The installer performs actions outside its documented purpose, including dropping hidden executables, modifying persistence mechanisms, and connecting to unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers should only install the intended application and its documented components, without creating hidden backdoors or modifying system persistence for unauthorized programs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some installers may install auto-updaters or supporting services, but these are documented, signed, and do not connect to unknown infrastructure.
key_indicators: Dropping hidden or unsigned executables during installation
Persistence via registry or scheduled task modification
Outbound connections to attacker infrastructure during or after install
Installer process spawning unauthorized child processes

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Shell script or binary downloaded from Pastebin/GitHub exploits vulnerabilities, installs cryptominer, and propagates to other systems.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code exploits known vulnerabilities to gain unauthorized access, downloads additional payloads from Pastebin or GitHub, installs a cryptominer on the compromised system, and scans the network for new targets to propagate itself, resulting in automated lateral movement and resource hijacking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automates exploitation of multiple CVEs, downloads and executes further payloads from public paste sites, installs unauthorized cryptomining software, and self-propagates across networks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not exploit vulnerabilities, download code from untrusted public sources, or self-replicate to other systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated update scripts may download code, but only from trusted, verified sources and without exploiting vulnerabilities or propagating themselves.
key_indicators: Automated exploitation of multiple known CVEs
Payload download from public paste sites (Pastebin, GitHub)
Installation and execution of cryptominer binaries

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is embedded in a trusted software update, installer, or downloaded payload (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll, VGCA installer, Gitpaste-12 worm).
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial compromise of the target system via supply chain or drive-by download.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, establishes persistence mechanisms, and initiates outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote control of the compromised system, data exfiltration, or further payload delivery.

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates sensitive data, executes attacker commands, installs additional payloads (e.g., cryptominers), or propagates to additional systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft, lateral movement within the network, or monetization through resource hijacking.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/S connections from trusted software (e.g., SolarWinds Orion, VGCA installer)
Installer processes dropping hidden or unsigned executables and modifying persistence settings (registry, scheduled tasks)
Automated exploitation of known vulnerabilities and self-propagation behavior (network scanning, exploit attempts)
Execution of cryptominer binaries by non-administrative processes
file_indicators: Modified or unsigned DLLs in SolarWinds Orion application directories (e.g., SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected hash or signature)
Unexpected executables dropped by installer processes in system or user directories
Shell scripts or binaries downloaded from Pastebin, GitHub, or other public paste sites
Persistence-related modifications (new registry run keys, scheduled tasks, or service entries) created by installer or update processes
network_indicators: Connections to known SUNBURST C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com and subdomains)
Outbound traffic to unknown IPs/domains during or after installation of trusted software
Frequent connections to Pastebin, GitHub, or similar services for payload download
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns from installer or update processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network connections from trusted applications, especially during or after installation or update. Inspect installer and update packages for unauthorized embedded executables, persistence mechanisms, or modified DLLs. Detect exploitation attempts and payload downloads from public paste sites by correlating process activity with network traffic. Use EDR and network monitoring to identify suspicious file drops, persistence changes, and outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure. Cross-reference file hashes and signatures of critical DLLs and executables against known-good baselines.
